thesis.title: Sticky subscription revenue that expands inside the customer base
thesis.text: Live subscription ARR reached £20.1m at March 2026, up 24% in the year, across 1,412 sites. FY2026 net revenue retention was 109% and gross revenue retention 93%: expansion of £2.6m more than offset £1.1m of churn and downgrades. Subscription is 75% of net revenue and carries an 81% software gross margin.

thesis.title: Payments attach is a second revenue engine on the same customers
thesis.text: Tidewell Pay was enabled at 60% of live sites in August 2026 (58% at March 2026 and 30% at March 2023) and processed £616.5m in FY2026 at a net take rate of 0.615%. Net payments revenue was £3.8m, 16% of net revenue, earned on customers who already pay for the software.

thesis.title: A funded route to breakeven in a market that is largely unpenetrated
thesis.text: A bottom-up serviceable market of £349m across 17,300 clinics in the UK, the Netherlands and Germany compares with 1,488 live sites today. The Series C funds product development and the German expansion, and management's forecast reaches positive adjusted EBITDA in FY2028, subject to the risks on Kinmoor and the German reseller.

risks.risk: Kinmoor Veterinary Group, the largest customer at about 11% of live ARR (212 sites), served written notice of non-renewal on 3 June 2026, effective 31 December 2026. The latest forecast (model v4.3) still assumes renewal at full value.
risks.mitigant: The Board has asked the CEO and the CRO to offer a three-year renewal at a 15% discount to current pricing; no offer has been accepted. The loan downside removes Kinmoor in full, and terms for any investor should be tested on a forecast that excludes it rather than on the management forecast.

risks.risk: The exclusive German reseller, Vetsana Handels GmbH, had 41 sites live at 30 June 2026 against a commitment of 150 by 31 March 2027, which needs about 12 go-lives a month. If it misses, Tidewell may convert the appointment to non-exclusive, and German growth then rests more on direct sales.
risks.mitigant: Tidewell holds the option to convert to non-exclusive if the minimum is missed, and Tidewell GmbH can sell directly. The Board asked for a recovery plan in March and reviewed progress in July; exclusivity otherwise runs to 31 December 2028.

risks.risk: The latest FY2027 forecast needs a second-half ramp well above the August run-rate after Q1 revenue came in 8% behind budget, and it assumes Kinmoor renews at full value. The FY2027 hiring plan costs more than the model carries.
risks.mitigant: Test returns, covenants and sizing on the downside cases in this record rather than on the management forecast; obtain the Q2 board pack and a reconciled hiring plan before final approval.

risks.risk: Cash was £10.9m at 31 August 2026 with £2.0m of the £5.0m revolving credit facility drawn. Runway is about 16 months on the March to August burn and 13 months net of the facility; at the current burn cash reaches the existing £3.0m minimum cash covenant in about 12 months.
risks.mitigant: The Series C is in process with a lead investor and exclusivity in place, the proposed loan would refinance the facility and add liquidity, and the Board asked in June for a monthly covenant forecast.

risks.risk: The CFO, Daniel Okafor, has resigned and leaves on 31 October 2026, during the Series C and before the FY2026 audit completes. A search for a successor is under way.
risks.mitigant: The Board has asked for an interim plan covering the audit and the round, and the Head of FP&A runs the model and the board pack. Make delivery of audited FY2026 accounts and a named finance lead conditions of completion.

risks.risk: Tidewell holds a SOC 2 Type I report issued on 14 May 2026. The Type II observation window runs from 1 June to 30 November 2026 and ISO 27001 is at readiness stage only. Group customers may require the stronger certification.
risks.mitigant: The Type II report is expected after the window closes; make it a post-completion undertaking and obtain the 2026 penetration test report, which is listed in the data room index but not provided.

risks.risk: At the proposed terms the Series C price per share is below the Series B price. The headline step-up in valuation is absorbed by the option pool top-up inside the pre-money, and the Series B broad-based weighted-average anti-dilution protection is triggered.
risks.mitigant: Quantify the Series B adjustment in the closing cap table. The effective pre-money for existing holders after the top-up is in this record, and price is a point to settle with the lead.

risks.risk: Tidewell Pay relies on its authorised e-money institution partner for acquiring and settlement. A change in the partner's status or terms would affect payments revenue, which is 16% of FY2026 net revenue and the main driver of attach.
risks.mitigant: Tidewell acts as registered agent under an existing arrangement. Review the agency agreement and the partner's terms in legal diligence.

risks.risk: A complaint to the Information Commissioner's Office was lodged in February 2025 about a 2024 incident and its outcome is pending. The legal questionnaire response does not mention it.
risks.mitigant: Request the ICO correspondence and current status, and seek a specific warranty and indemnity from the company.

narrative.company_description: Tidewell is a Bristol-based software business serving veterinary practices in the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Germany. Tidewell Practice is a cloud practice management system covering appointments, clinical records, stock and invoicing. Tidewell Pay adds card payments inside the same workflow and operates as the registered agent of an authorised e-money institution, so Tidewell does not hold client money. Founded in 2017 and still led by its two co-founders, the group served 503 customers across 1,488 live sites at 31 August 2026 and employed 226 people. Revenue is recognised net of payment pass-through costs: FY2026 net revenue was £24.0m, of which 75% was subscription.
narrative.market: Tidewell's bottom-up serviceable market is £349m a year across 17,300 clinics: 5,200 in the UK, 1,100 in the Netherlands and 11,000 in Germany. It is built from software at £14.5k per clinic a year (£251m) plus payments at a net take rate of 0.615% on £77k of monthly volume per site (£98m). Tidewell's 1,488 live sites are about 9% of that clinic universe, so most of the opportunity is unpenetrated, but it is concentrated in Germany, where growth depends on an exclusive reseller that is behind its site commitment.

series_c_terms.text: Series C Preferred Shares of £0.0001 each, convertible 1:1 into Ordinary Shares.
In priority to all other shares: the greater of 1x the original issue price plus declared dividends and the amount receivable on conversion (non-participating).
Broad-based weighted average, with customary exceptions for the option pool.
Unallocated pool increased before completion to 8% of the fully diluted share capital after completion. The increase is inside the pre-money valuation.
The lead may appoint one director; the board is up to seven directors including an independent chair.
Changes to share rights, new senior securities, borrowing above the consent threshold in the record, and any sale of the company.
Existing shareholders may sell up to £6.0m of shares to the investors at a 15% discount to the original issue price, conditional on completion of the primary issue.
New service agreements with 12-month non-compete and non-solicit; no re-vesting of founder shares.
Satisfactory due diligence, delivery of audited consolidated accounts for the year ended 31 March 2026, lead investor committee approval, new articles and customary warranties.
45 days from countersignature; the company pays the lead's reasonable costs up to £150,000 plus VAT.
Draft v3 dated 22 September 2026; non-binding save for exclusivity, costs, confidentiality and governing law.

growth_loan.summary: A senior secured growth term loan to Tidewell, repaying and cancelling the existing revolving credit facility at completion: 36 months, interest-only for the first 12, then equal monthly principal instalments, priced over SONIA with an arrangement fee and warrants.
growth_loan.borrower: Tidewell Software Ltd, guaranteed by Tidewell Group Holdings Limited
security: First-ranking debenture over all assets of Tidewell Software Ltd and Tidewell Group Holdings Limited, replacing the existing debenture on repayment of the revolving credit facility.
Cross-guarantee from Tidewell Group Holdings Limited and Tidewell Software Ltd.
Share pledges over the Dutch and German subsidiaries are not proposed at this stage.
conditions_precedent: Repayment in full and cancellation of the existing revolving credit facility and release of its security.
Satisfactory legal, financial and commercial diligence, including a written update on Kinmoor.
Consent of the Series C investors to the borrowing, where required by the protective provisions.
Delivery of audited consolidated accounts for the year ended 31 March 2026.
Confirmation of finance leadership after the CFO's departure.
Executed warrant instrument, security documents and know-your-customer checks.

covenant_definitions.definition: Cash at bank at each month end; tested monthly from the first month end after completion.
Live subscription ARR as defined in this record, excluding contracted-not-live; tested monthly.

growth_loan.downside_definition: Kinmoor leaves on 31 December 2026 (net of any retained sites) and the German reseller adds sites at half the pace needed for its 150-site minimum. Neither the downside nor the base case includes Series C proceeds, so the covenants are tested as a stand-alone credit.
growth_loan.grade_rationale: Recurring-revenue business with good gross retention, but one customer notice, a thin stand-alone cash path in the downside, a pending equity round and a finance-leadership gap.

rows: Repay the revolving credit facility drawn balance
sources_uses.note: The undrawn part of the existing facility is cancelled on refinancing.

columns.label: Base case: lowest in 12 test months

covenants.note: Cash headroom is measured on pro forma cash at 31 December 2026; ARR headroom on the latest live ARR. Both cases exclude Series C proceeds.

amortisation.note: Interest-only for the first months, then equal principal instalments; interest at one twelfth of the all-in rate on the opening balance.

downside_path.note: Aug-26 is actual. The loan completes at the end of Dec-26 and covenants are tested monthly from Jan-27. Neither case includes Series C proceeds.

rows: Monthly ARR growth in both cases (FY2026 compound rate)
Monthly net cash burn at Aug-26 (March to August average)
Incremental cash margin on ARR growth (management FY2027 to FY2028 forecast)
Gross margin applied to ARR lost in the downside (FY2026 blended)
Kinmoor ARR removed from January 2027, net of retained sites
German go-lives a month needed to reach the minimum by 31 March 2027
German ramp in the downside as a share of the required pace
Net ARR per German reseller site after the 30% reseller margin
downside_assumptions.note: German ARR per site is a deal-team assumption: £12,000 gross, smaller than the UK average, less the 30% reseller margin.

secondary.summary: A secondary buyer purchases shares from early holders at a discount to the Series C price, conditional on completion of the primary issue.
secondary.seller_selection: Sellers are the pre-Series A holders: the CEO (half), the seed investor and the early employees and angels. All three hold shares that rank behind the later preferred classes.
notes: The secondary is conditional on completion of the primary issue and does not change the fully diluted share count.
Ordinary and Seed Preferred shares are acquired. The draft term sheet does not say whether they are re-designated into Series C Preferred on transfer; this is an open point.
GBP deal data is converted at the planning rate stated in the record, not the billing rate.

sellers.note: Sellers are early holders; the CEO provides half. Shares sold at the secondary price. Founder and employee shares are Ordinary; the angels hold Seed Preferred.
